column1: # Phase 4 milestone D follow-up: the scheduled fluid-tick loop's golden run
# parameters.
# NOT a vanilla dump: `tests/fluid_test.cpp` pins the state encoding and each
# branch of `fluid_tick` one call at a time, but nothing there runs the loop.
# `ctest -R fluid_tick` replays every row below through the real
# `FluidTickQueue` and the real dispatch (`run_fluid_tick_position`'s shape: the
# schedule callback rebound to the entry's own kind, then `fluid_tick`), and
# compares the whole trace line for line, so a write that moved, a schedule one
# tick early or an entry that silently ran cannot land.
# There is no seed column. `fluid_tick` takes no draw at all — its stream is a
# function of the world and the two constants `fluid_drop_off` (1 water, 2
# lava) and `fluid_tick_delay` (5 and 30) — so unlike the fire dump there is no
# level stream whose state belongs to the server, and this trace is the whole
# stream rather than a sampled part of it.
# `ticks` is how many world ticks the run advanced the queue through (one
# `advance()` each), `schedules`/`due`/`stales`/`writes`/`reads` are the counts
# of those trace rows — `reads` is one row per world read, and a dispatch
# makes exactly one per cell it asks about — and `endNow`/`endPending` the
# queue's own state after the last tick — a run that settles is zero (the rule
# only re-queues a cell that actually moved, so a settled pool stops ticking
# itself), and every run here does. `rows` is the trace's length.
